newsitem.title: USA: Ill. school district gets extension for COPs sale.
newsitem.headline: Ill. school district gets extension for COPs sale.

text.p: An Illinois school district has gotten a reprieve from a yearend, court-ordered deadline to issue nearly $50 million of certificates of participation, a school official said Friday.
Matthew Corby, associate superintendent of management services for the Rockford School District, said a U.S. District Court judge had staid his order requiring the debt sale by Jan. 31.

Instead, Corby said he believed the district now had until the end of January to complete the sale ordered by the court as part of an ongoing desegregation case. Proceeds from the COPs will be used to finance three new buildings.

In the meantime, the district is waiting to hear from Banc One Capital Corp. and Financial Security Assurance about a financial plan the district submitted to the court earlier this month, Corby said.
The district, which is working with Banc One on the COPs sale, hopes to obtain insurance for the deal from FSA, he added.
The judge ordered the district to come up with a plan for dealing with its reoccuring operating deficits. The district currently has a $15 million deficit in its $200 million fiscal 1997 budget.
Corby said that under the five-year plan, the district's budget would be balanced starting in the third year through a series of personnel and service cuts.
